body:
pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered: GPU provisioner high queue length for prod-gpu-pool. Alert: inference-queue > 1200 reqs, average wait 18s, tail latency 4200ms. severity: P1

alice: I'm oncall. seeing steady growth on the queue; autoscaler reports repeated AddNode failures. Paging infra-sre.

ben: joining. k8s event stream shows: FailedCreatePod -> insufficient resources: Request for GPU but no nodes. Autoscaler logs: 'scaledown/scaleup attempt failed: LaunchTemplate mismatch or unauthorized to attach instance profile'.

carol: I pulled the autoscaler logs — showing 403 from EC2: "UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole is not allowed" when creating nodegroup with launch-template version v5. CAS attempts to create nodes with new launch template that references the new instance profile.

dave: Confirmed — we rolled a launch template update earlier for AMI patch and drifted instance profile role name. New LT refers to role 'redwood-gpu-node-role-v2' but the autoscaler IAM role still allows passrole for 'redwood-gpu-node-role'. so upstream API rejects.

alice: Customer impact? eve pls check support funnel and top 5 customers on prod cluster.

eve: Noted. Two high-volume customers (search-sim and chat-ops) report timeouts and increased 429 throttles. Support has queued ~8 customer tickets marked "degraded". Escalating to CS.

ben: Mitigation path 1 (fast): manually scale existing dedicated GPU nodegroup (pool-a) from 12 -> 18 to drain queue while we fix IAM. This uses available EC2 quota. Any objections?

carol: I'll try a manual scale. But kube-autoscaler may immediately try to create nodes in the misconfigured nodegroup if we don't pause it.

alice: Put autoscaler into maintenance mode: annotate cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true? Wait that's scale-down. For scale-up pause we can set env var or temporarily scale the autoscaler deployment to 0?

ben: Easiest: kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0. I'll do it and then manually increase nodegroup.

alice: Do it. Also create an incident channel for comms.

pagerduty-bot: alice acknowledged the incident.

ben: running: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-a --desired-capacity 18
```

carol: Autoscaler stopped. Scaling ASG now. ASG responded OK, new instances booting. AMI health checks ok. Node registration is slow because kubelet can't join until kubelet IAM profile attaches.

dave: While those nodes come up, we should create a short-term fallback: route lowest-latency customers to smaller CPU-backed pool (prod-fallback-cpu) with graceful degradation to 0.75x model. We can update routing policy in the serving router.

alice: Agree. dave take lead on routing change. ben continue manual scale and start an IAM mitigation (temp policy). carol please open a ticket to fix launch template + instance profile mapping permanently.

ben: Quick IAM mitigation: add iam:PassRole permission for the autoscaler role to the new role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-gpu-node-role-v2. Applying policy now.

ben: Applied. Verifying with aws sts:simulate-principal-policy returned allowed for PassRole on target.

carol: Re-enable autoscaler: kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=2

ben: Autoscaler resumed. Observed CreateFleet/CreateFleet instances succeed now. New nodes join and kubelet registers. Kube events: Node gpu-12.ready, gpu-13.ready, gpu-14.ready.

alice: Monitor queue and latencies. dave, how's traffic routing?

dave: Router change pushed: traffic split 80/20 to fallback CPU for the top slow routes. Model downgraded with prompt-preservation. Expect 20% of requests to have lower quality but latency bound protected.

eve: Notifying impacted customers that we have degraded routing and mitigation in place. Triage notes added to support tickets.

ben: Queue length dropping from 1200 -> 300 over the last 9 minutes. tail latency back to ~600ms. 429 errors down.

carol: Opening follow-up action items: 1) Reconcile launch template versions across ASGs, 2) Update autoscaler policy to include iam:PassRole for new node role naming scheme, 3) Add preflight check in LT CI to ensure IAM role exists, 4) Add guardrail to catch launch-template->instance-profile drift.

alice: Handing off to ben for postmortem and follow-up. I'm walking off-call in 30m; ben you take the incident lead. ben ack?

ben: Ack. Will own oncall follow-ups and coordinate with security for IAM policy change review.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved and silenced. Root cause: autoscaler attempted to create nodes with updated launch template referencing an instance profile not allowed by autoscaler IAM role (iam:PassRole missing). Secondary impact: queue growth while scale-up failed, causing throttles and degraded customer experience. Mitigations: manual ASG scale, temporary iam:PassRole grant, cluster-autoscaler restart, routing fallback to CPU pool.

alice: Thanks all. We'll run retro tomorrow. Add timeline and logs to the incident doc: /incidents/2468013579/notes.

ben: Uploading logs and commands used to the incident doc. Also adding the exact IAM policy diff, ASG size changes, and routing commit hash.

carol: I'll schedule the LT reconciliation runbook and PR.

eve: Customers notified with ETA for full restoration and link to status page.

alice: Closing thread after postmortem. Good work. :thumbsup:
